issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit interEdit and MultiEdit interpret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patternspret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patterns

steps:
Create a file named split_lines.sh in the current directory with exactly the following content (keep every character as given):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# split_lines.sh: print every field of the first argument on its own line
IFS=,
read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
  echo "[$p]"
done
In split_lines.sh, change only the line `IFS=,` to `IFS=$'\n'` so the fields are split on newlines instead of commas. Do not change any other line.
expected: Edit writes new_string literally, so line 3 becomes `IFS=$'\n'` and the other six lines are unchanged.
defect: Edit interprets `$'` in new_string as a String.prototype.replace substitution pattern, so the file becomes 'IFS=' + all content from original line 4 + "\n'" + another copy of that content (7 -> 12 lines, bash 'unexpected EOF'), while the tool reports completed and the preview shows the correct `IFS=$'\n'`.

fault location.explanation: In non-replace_all mode the edit uses content.replace(oldString, newString) with a string replacement, so `$'`, `$&`, `` $` `` and `$$` in new_string are expanded as substitution patterns instead of being written literally.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). Edit and MultiEdit share applyEditToContent in src/tools/editCore.ts. When replace_all is false it computes `content.replace(oldString, newString)`; with a string as the second argument, JavaScript's String.prototype.replace treats `$'` as "the portion of the string after the match", `` $` `` as the portion before, `$&` as the match and `$$` as a single `$`. Replacing `IFS=,` with `IFS=$'\n'` therefore inserts the remainder of the file (from line 4) in place of `$'`, followed by the literal `\n'`, then the original remainder again, turning 7 lines into 12 and breaking the script. The function returns replacements=1 and the preview is built from the raw new_string, so the tool reports success with a correct-looking diff. The replace_all branch (split/join) is not affected. Minimal fix: use a replacer function so the text is inserted literally, e.g. `content.replace(oldString, () => newString)` (or slice by indexOf), on line 68.
